  rationale: It is the only functional feature Plus adds per [REDACTED:high_entropy]; if it is allowed to slip to should-have under build pressure, the monetization decision from that phase becomes unbuildable and Plus has zero differentiation.
  rejected: Leaving per-deck reminder customization as an implicit detail under the general Free/Plus requirement
  constraints: Build phase must implement per-deck reminder-time customization as a gating must-have, not a stretch goal
- [DEC-app_features-003] Every must-have acceptance criterion must be independently executable by a human or script to a pass/fail result — restating the feature description is not an acceptance criterion.
  rationale: Without this discipline, 'acceptance criteria' risk becoming decorative prose that can't actually gate a build-verification pass, undermining the project's 'provably right, not plausibly right' standard.
  rejected: Accepting qualitative/descriptive acceptance criteria for must-have features
  constraints: Requirements-json entries and later build verification must map to concrete, checkable tests or scripted scenarios
- [DEC-app_features-004] Two new concrete acceptance checks are added to the must-have gate: CSV test fixtures must include at least one real-world exported file (not only hand-crafted edge cases), and hitting a Free-tier cap mid-review-session must not corrupt or block the in-progress session.
  rationale: The first operationalizes [REDACTED:high_entropy] into a testable gate rather than a suggestion; the second closes a previously unstated interaction between monetization caps and the review-flow-speed priority, which the fixed SM-2>speed>honesty tiebreaker (DEC-prompt_contract-007) requires be protected.
  rejected: Treating real-world CSV fixtures as a nice-to-have rather than a gating test; Leaving cap-during-review behavior unspecified and discovering it as a bug during build
  constraints: Build/test phase must source or construct a real-world CSV fixture and include a cap-hit-mid-session test case
- [DEC-app_features-005] The 3-tab information architecture (already locked structurally in [REDACTED:high_entropy]) is scored as should-have rather than must-have within this phase's MoSCoW prioritization, meaning it does not itself gate 'done' even though it will be built as the locked navigational shell.
  rationale: MoSCoW scoring in this phase measures what gates completion under time pressure, not what is architecturally decided; the IA is already structurally locked and not actually at risk of being cut, so should-have scoring reflects prioritization nuance, not a reopening of the IA decision.
  rejected: Scoring 3-tab IA as must-have, duplicating the prior lock as a redundant gate
  constraints: The 3-tab IA decision itself remains locked per [REDACTED:high_entropy]; should-have scoring here is about build-priority sequencing only, not about whether it gets built
- [DEC-design_discussion-001] Design language is named 'The Honest Ledger': a calm, information-dense, non-gamified visual language (tabular numerals for counts, ink/graphite palette with a single reserved amber accent used only for due-today badges and confirmed-save moments).
  rationale: Codex and Claude independently converged on the same underlying philosophy (precision-instrument trust over engagement/gamification); Claude's persona-grounded framing and concrete palette were adopted as the more specific, buildable version of the same direction.
  rejected: Codex's 'Scheduled Trust Instrument' naming (same philosophy, folded in rather than kept as a separate competing name); Generic 'clean and modern' non-answer; Gamified/streak-flame/confetti visual register
  constraints: Any later phase or build artifact must reference this name and palette rationale, not invent a new unrelated design language
- [DEC-design_discussion-002] The default-looking version of this app (plain List rows, stock Form, system blue accent, color-only grade pills, generic unlabeled charts, post-grade 'Saved!' toast) is explicitly rejected with five named concrete replacements: custom due-count deck cards, ascending-staircase shape/position/label-based grading buttons, ink/graphite+amber palette with no system blue, directly-labeled 'today' bar in the forecast chart, and structural (not toast-based) save confirmation.
  rationale: The phase rules require explicit rejection of the default look with named differences, not adjectives; the toast-banner rejection is additionally a correctness requirement, not just aesthetic preference, since a 'Saved' banner mid-session risks implying false session completion.
  rejected: Default SwiftUI List/Form/TabView chrome; Color-only (red/orange/green/blue) grading buttons with no shape/label distinction; A green 'Saved!' toast/banner shown after each grade
  constraints: No screen may ship with default unstyled List/Form chrome where this spec calls for custom rows/cards; No completion-implying confirmation UI (toast, banner, checkmark overlay) may appear after a single grade during an active session
- [DEC-design_discussion-003] Signature interaction is the reveal-and-grade motion: a fast (<200ms), no-bounce content settle on tap-to-reveal (explicitly not a 3D card-flip), paired with four grade buttons rising from the bottom edge, each with a distinct haptic weight on an ascending ladder from Again to Easy.
  rationale: Expresses the design language's calm/trust register while protecting review-flow speed (priority #2); a literal card-flip looks nice once but is fatiguing by the fortieth card of a session, and the haptic ladder lets grading work by feel for a user reviewing one-handed on a moving train.
  rejected: A literal 3D card-flip reveal animation; Uniform/no haptic feedback across all four grade buttons
  constraints: Reduced-motion accessibility setting must disable the reveal-settle animation but must not remove the haptic ladder, since haptics are not motion
- [DEC-design_discussion-004] Screen inventory is locked across the existing 3-tab shell: Study (Deck List w/ due counts + Study All + empty/all-caught-up states; Deck Detail; Card Editor sheet with keyboard-first flow; Review Session; Session Summary reachable only on full completion), Stats (Overview + per-deck drill-down, each with distinct empty/sparse/success states), Settings & Tools (root list; CSV Export; CSV Import with per-row status preview; Reminders with tri-state permission handling and per-deck Plus override; Demo Data toggle; Plan/Subscription screen; Gap & Limitations register as its own real screen).
  rationale: Both substantive contributors independently produced nearly identical screen inventories mapped onto the already-locked 3-tab IA; Claude's version added concrete detail (Study All entry, cap-hit-mid-session as inline notice not modal, Gap register as a first-class readable screen rather than a buried settings row) that Codex did not contradict.
  rejected: Burying the Gap & Limitations register inside a generic settings row rather than giving it its own screen; A modal interruption for the cap-hit-mid-session case
  constraints: Build phase must implement each listed screen with the state model specified in DEC-design_discussion-005; The Gap & Limitations register must be reachable as its own discoverable screen, not nested prose in an About page
- [DEC-design_discussion-005] Per-screen state models are locked, including two new explicit substates beyond prior phases' requirements: Deck List gets a distinct 'all caught up' success substate separate from true empty, and Review Session gets a 'cap hit mid-session' state rendered as a small non-blocking inline notice rather than a modal.
  rationale: A true-empty state ('you have no decks yet') and an 'all caught up' state ('you have decks but nothing is due') communicate very different things and deserve different copy; rendering the cap-hit state as a modal would itself violate the locked requirement that hitting a cap must not corrupt or interrupt an in-progress review session.
  rejected: Reusing one generic empty-state graphic for both true-empty and all-caught-up cases; A modal/blocking alert for the cap-hit-mid-session case
  constraints: Stats screens must never render a chart from fabricated-looking flat placeholder data even in the sparse state
- [DEC-design_discussion-006] Accessibility requirements for this phase are locked as: grading buttons satisfy the non-color-dependent requirement specifically via the shape/position/label staircase (not a later-added tooltip); card front/back text scales with Dynamic Type including accessibility sizes via a scrolling card area, with the grade-button area reserved in the bottom safe zone; charts carry Swift Charts accessibility summary labels.
  rationale: Claude flagged that the staircase/haptic-ladder approach is more visually and technically interesting than four equal buttons and risks being treated as stretch polish and cut under build-time pressure, when it is in fact how the already-locked non-color-dependent grading requirement gets satisfied.
  rejected: Treating the staircase layout as optional visual polish rather than the accessibility requirement's actual implementation; Letting Dynamic Type growth push grade buttons off-screen
  constraints: Build phase may not substitute a plain tooltip or color-only fallback for the staircase layout and call the accessibility requirement satisfied
- [DEC-design_handoff-001] A single canonical token set (type scale, spacing grid, color palette, corner radii) is locked from Codex's fuller semantic palette (covers surfaceMuted/Elevated, textTertiary, chartGrid, focusOutline — roles Claude's independently-derived palette didn't name), reconciling it with Claude's compatible-but-different hex values.
  rationale: Both contributors produced complete, numerically-specified specs in the same direction (Honest Ledger, ink/graphite/amber) but with different exact hex values since they worked independently; a build needs one canonical file, not two options.
  rejected: Shipping Claude's palette instead (fewer named semantic roles for required categories like chart grid and focus outline); Leaving both palettes in the handoff for the builder to choose
  constraints: Theme.swift must be built from the values in this phase's Final Output only, with zero invented values; No color/font/spacing literal may appear outside Theme.swift
- [DEC-design_handoff-002] Component inventory is merged into one canonical named list, with three components explicitly flagged as their own files that must not be reimplemented ad hoc: GradeStaircase (neutral ink/graphite only, no per-grade color), DemoDataTag (one reusable component used everywhere demo content appears), and InlineCapNotice (persistent, non-blocking, shaped distinctly from anything toast-like).
  rationale: Both contributors independently converged on nearly the same component set; the explicit do-not-regress flag on these three specifically protects already-locked accessibility (DEC-design_discussion-006) and correctness (no false-completion signal) requirements that are easy for a builder to quietly erode under time pressure.
  rejected: Leaving component boundaries implicit and letting the builder infer which pieces are load-bearing vs. cosmetic
  constraints: A future change adding per-grade color tinting or a toast-style save confirmation is a regression against this decision, not a style choice
- [DEC-design_handoff-003] Navigation is locked as three independent per-tab NavigationStacks; Review Session pushes onto the Study stack (not a sheet) and hides the tab bar for its duration; Card Editor, CSV Import, and Plan/Subscription present as sheets; Session Summary is a sheet reachable only after true queue completion; the in-session exit control reads 'End session — your progress is saved' rather than a loss-warning dialog.
  rationale: Claude's specific mechanism (push + hidden tab bar to protect focus during the highest-stakes flow) refines Codex's less specific navigation description without contradicting it; the honest exit-copy detail is required because, given the locked interruption-safety architecture, a loss-warning dialog would literally be lying to the user.
  rejected: Presenting Review Session as a sheet; A confirmation dialog warning the user they might lose progress by leaving early
  constraints: Build phase must implement the exit control's copy exactly as specified, since it is a correctness statement, not just UX copy
- [DEC-design_handoff-004] Review Session must snapshot an ordered array of due Card IDs once at session start and step through it by index — it must NOT be driven by a live SwiftData @Query.
  rationale: A live query re-triggers on every grade (since grading mutates dueDate), which can reorder or shrink the visible queue mid-session, especially in Study All mode across multiple decks — this would look exactly like a data-loss bug even though the underlying data is safe, and it is the kind of subtle pitfall a builder would introduce by reaching for the 'obviously idiomatic' SwiftUI pattern.
  rejected: Driving the review queue directly off a live @Query for simplicity
  constraints: Build/test phase must include a Study-All multi-deck test that would catch queue reordering if this constraint is violated
- [DEC-design_handoff-005] Interruption-safety is implemented as 'recompute the due query fresh from truth on relaunch' rather than an explicit session save/restore mechanism; there is no separate persisted resume-point.
  rationale: Because each grade is already synchronously saved and updates the card's dueDate immediately, a fresh due-query on relaunch automatically excludes graded cards and automatically includes ungraded ones — building a separate resume-state mechanism would add its own bug surface for no benefit and risks a path by which a fabricated summary could appear.
  rejected: Persisting and restoring an explicit session/resume-point object
  constraints: The force-quit test scenario should verify this by killing mid-session and confirming the relaunched due query alone produces the correct graded/ungraded split, not a restored session object
- [DEC-design_handoff-006] SwiftData schema is finalized as Deck/Card/ReviewLog with the fields specified; Card.isDemo is a denormalized copy from its parent Deck at creation time (not derived via join), due status is a computed predicate against a freshly-computed 'start of tomorrow' instant (never a stored boolean), and ReviewLog rows are strictly append-only and never mutated in place.
  rationale: This is the concrete implementation of the calendar-day-at-query-time rule (DEC-prompt_contract-002) and the cloud-readiness immutable-event-log intent ([REDACTED:high_entropy]); denormalizing isDemo avoids an expensive join on every stats aggregation at the 300-3,000 card scale this persona lives at, and append-only ReviewLog prevents a future 'quick bug fix' from silently breaking the immutable-history guarantee.
  rejected: Deriving isDemo via a join to Deck on every query; Storing due status as a mutable boolean flag; Allowing in-place correction of ReviewLog rows
  constraints: Build phase must enforce ReviewLog immutability at the architecture level (e.g., no update path exposed), not just as a convention
- [DEC-design_handoff-007] Per-grade save runs synchronously on the main actor against the live ModelContext; this is an accepted, explicitly named performance cost (a possible small stutter on old devices), not something to defer to a background save.
  rationale: This is the mechanism that actually closes the interruption-safety guarantee ([REDACTED:high_entropy]); backgrounding the save for a smoother feel would silently reopen the exact data-loss window the app's entire trust claim depends on closing, and given the SM-2-correctness-then-speed-then-honesty tiebreaker, correctness wins this specific tradeoff.
  rejected: Moving the per-grade save to a background queue/actor for smoother perceived performance
  constraints: Any future performance optimization pass must not move this save off the synchronous main-actor path
- [DEC-design_handoff-008] Local reminders use repeats:false, re-scheduled (remove-pending then re-add for 'tomorrow') at each of the four locked refresh points; gap-register copy should describe a skipped day as the notification 'never being created,' not merely 'stale.'
  rationale: A UNCalendarNotificationTrigger's body text is fixed at schedule time, so repeats:true would freeze a due-count forever; this refines the already-locked staleness-acceptance decision ([REDACTED:high_entropy]) with the actual technically-accurate framing for the gap register.
  rejected: Using repeats:true with a fixed body text; Keeping the vaguer 'staleness' framing instead of the more accurate 'never created' framing
  constraints: Gap & Limitations screen copy must use the 'never created if app unopened between days' framing
- [DEC-design_handoff-009] The four-step haptic ladder is concretely mapped onto iOS's actual 5 discrete UIImpactFeedbackGenerator styles as Again=.light, Hard=.medium, Good=.heavy, Easy=.heavy+a second .light pulse — resolving the fact that iOS's styles (light/medium/heavy/soft/rigid) are not a clean linear intensity scale.
  rationale: Codex's original light/medium/rigid/heavy mapping doesn't reliably read as an ascending ladder since rigid and heavy differ in feel-character more than magnitude; Claude's fix gives Easy a distinctly 'extra' top-of-ladder feel using only real, available iOS haptic primitives.
  rejected: The original light/medium/rigid/heavy mapping; Inventing a fifth intensity level iOS doesn't provide
  constraints: Haptic ladder must be validated on a physical device before considered done — Simulator playback is not representative
- [DEC-design_handoff-010] No external Claude Design pass is used by default; the spec's explicit numeric values are sufficient for direct SwiftUI implementation. A ready-to-use Claude Design prompt is preserved for optional use only if the run is configured to pause for external design or a limited palette sanity-check is wanted.
  rationale: Every token has a real number and every component is named/mapped; the actual risk in this app is native SwiftUI fidelity (Dynamic Type, safe areas, VoiceOver, haptic timing), not visual concepting, so an external design round would only add reverse-engineering risk without reducing any real uncertainty.
  rejected: Always running a full external Claude Design mockup pass across all 13 screens
  constraints: If external design is invoked, it is scoped to at most Deck List and Review Session as a sanity-check, not a full handoff replacing this document
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] App architecture is three layers: a pure domain package (SM-2 engine + CSV parser, zero SwiftUI/SwiftData imports, no direct Date()/Calendar.current calls) as its own local Swift package target, a thin SwiftData repository layer, and SwiftUI + @Observable presentation view models.
  rationale: Physical package separation (not just file-organization convention) is the only thing that reliably prevents a future 'quick fix' from reaching for Date()/Calendar.current directly and silently invalidating the DST/timezone test matrix; it also keeps SM-2 and CSV logic independently testable and provably pure.
  rejected: Keeping SM-2/CSV as plain files inside the main app target with a style-guide convention against impure calls; A single monolithic app target with MVVM only, no package boundary
  constraints: SM-2 and CSV modules must have zero imports of SwiftUI, SwiftData, or Foundation's Date()/Calendar.current singletons — only injected Clock/Calendar values
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Apple framework set is locked to SwiftUI, SwiftData, Swift Charts, StoreKit 2, UserNotifications, UniformTypeIdentifiers, OSLog, Swift Testing, and XCUITest; no ML/CoreML/ARKit or any other framework is introduced.
  rationale: Every locked feature in this app is served by this exact set; nothing in the requirements justifies machine learning, augmented reality, or any framework outside this list, and stating this plainly now prevents tech_specs from re-litigating it.
  rejected: ML-based scheduling, OCR/handwriting card creation, or card-similarity features using CoreML
  constraints: Any framework outside this list requires explicit justification in tech_specs and must still pass the zero-ML/AR non-goal
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] ModelContainer initialization must include real error handling with a user-facing recovery screen (retry or explicit start-fresh option) rather than try!, and VersionedSchema/SchemaMigrationPlan scaffolding is set up from v1 even though there is only one schema version today.
  rationale: A try!-based ModelContainer init crash-loops on a corrupted store or failed lightweight migration, which for an app whose entire promise is 'never lose your progress' would be the single worst possible failure mode; setting up migration scaffolding now costs nothing but is the only thing standing between a future required field addition and silently corrupting existing users' ReviewLog history.
  rejected: Default try! ModelContainer initialization; Deferring migration-plan scaffolding until a second schema version is actually needed
  constraints: Build verification must include a test or manual check that a corrupted/unopenable store produces the recovery screen, not a crash
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Exactly one ModelContainer instance exists for the app's entire lifetime, not one per scene or window.
  rationale: Multiple containers/contexts racing on the same underlying store is a real risk under iPad multitasking or any future multi-window scenario, and is trivially avoided by a single shared instance.
  rejected: Per-scene ModelContainer instances
  constraints: Build phase must wire a single app-level ModelContainer, injected via environment, not recreated per view/scene
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The force-quit mid-session interruption test — the single most important test in the app — must be an automated, CI-runnable XCUITest using app.terminate() (a real SIGKILL) at a timed point around the synchronous save, asserting the exact graded/ungraded split on relaunch.
  rationale: A manual-only 'kill the simulator mid-session' QA step bit-rots and can silently stop being performed; app.terminate() is the actual sanctioned XCUITest mechanism for this and must be scripted so 'provably right' doesn't quietly become 'we tried it once.'
  rejected: Treating the force-quit test as a manual QA checklist item performed once before ship
  constraints: This test must exist as a checked-in, CI-runnable XCUITest, not documentation of a manual procedure
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] A Privacy Manifest (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) is a required build-verification checklist item despite the app having zero network calls.
  rationale: Apple's privacy manifest requirement is keyed on API usage categories (e.g. UserDefaults, file timestamps), not network usage, so a zero-network app can still trip App Store review without one; naming this now avoids a late-stage rejection surprise.
  rejected: Assuming a zero-network app doesn't need a privacy manifest
  constraints: Build verification checklist must include confirming PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is present and accurate before submission
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The notification permission prompt fires only when the user actively enables Reminders in Settings, never at cold launch.
  rationale: A denied first-ask at cold launch is much harder to recover from than a contextual ask tied to the user's own action, and this is also better UX consistent with the app's non-nagging tone.
  rejected: Requesting notification permission at first app launch
  constraints: Build phase must gate the UNUserNotificationCenter authorization request behind the user toggling Reminders on, not app launch
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] StoreKit implementation requires a checked-in .storekit configuration file with scripted expire/refund/renewal tests, a paywall carrying privacy-policy and terms-of-use links (App Review 3.1.2 requirement for auto-renewing subscriptions), and an explicit bounded error state (not a hang) when a purchase is attempted while offline.
  rationale: These are concrete, easily-missed requirements: the .storekit file makes subscription states testable in Simulator without a sandbox account; the policy/terms links are an actual Apple review requirement, not a nicety; and the offline-purchase case is the one real network touch in an otherwise offline app, so leaving it as a silent spinner would violate the app's own honesty principle.
  rejected: Testing StoreKit only against a live sandbox account; Leaving the offline-purchase-tap case as an indefinite loading spinner
  constraints: Build phase must include a checked-in .storekit config and scripted Xcode StoreKit testing scenarios for expire/refund/renew; Paywall screen must link to privacy policy and terms of use; Purchase flow must show a clear, bounded error message when attempted with no connectivity
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] CSV import must wrap file reads from the document picker in startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()/stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource().
  rationale: Document-picker URLs are security-scoped; omitting this pattern works fine in development (same process/session) and then intermittently fails for real users pulling files from iCloud Drive or other Files providers — a classic bug that's easy to miss until it ships.
  rejected: Reading the picked file URL directly without security-scoped access calls
  constraints: CSV import implementation must call start/stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource around every file read from the document picker
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Zero third-party dependencies is reaffirmed as a hard rule; the CSV parser is hand-rolled rather than sourced from any SPM package.
  rationale: The app already has a locked, exhaustive per-row CSV error taxonomy that a generic library wasn't designed around, so hand-rolling is actually less work than fighting someone else's abstraction, while keeping supply-chain surface at zero.
  rejected: Adopting a third-party CSV parsing library, even a permissively-licensed one
  constraints: No new SPM dependency may be added without explicit one-line justification per the approved tech stack policy, and CSV parsing specifically stays hand-rolled
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The Gap & Limitations screen requires its own automated test asserting the screen renders and contains the required disclosure strings (StoreKit exception, notification staleness/never-created framing, timezone-crossing due flips, iCloud backup divergence, full non-goals list).
  rationale: Without an automated check, 'must be documented' is exactly the kind of soft requirement that quietly disappears under time pressure with nobody able to prove it was actually shipped.
  rejected: Relying on manual review to confirm the Gap & Limitations content is present
  constraints: Test suite must include an assertion that the Gap & Limitations screen contains each required disclosure string
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Testing strategy is layered: Swift Testing unit tests for pure domain logic (SM-2, day-boundary/timezone predicates, CSV row classification, cap-hit logic), persistence tests against an in-memory SwiftData container for CRUD/cascade-delete/append-only ReviewLog behavior, integration tests for interruption/reminders/CSV flows, and UI tests paired with deterministic non-UI tests so correctness never depends on animation timing.
  rationale: This maps every locked correctness guarantee (SM-2 purity, interruption safety, CSV never-silently-drop, ReviewLog immutability) to a concrete, appropriately-scoped test layer rather than leaving test strategy as an afterthought discovered during build.
  rejected: Relying primarily on UI tests for correctness verification; Testing persistence only against the real on-device store rather than an in-memory container
  constraints: tech_specs and build phases must map each locked correctness requirement to one of these four test layers explicitly
- [DEC-tech_specs-001] Architecture is concretely implemented as two local Swift packages (RecallScheduling, RecallCSV) for pure domain logic plus an app-target SwiftData repository layer and SwiftUI+@Observable presentation, giving the already-locked three-layer architecture a specific file/module layout.
  rationale: Codex and Claude independently produced compatible, near-identical package/module breakdowns; making it concrete now (not just 'physically separate' in prose) is what actually lets parallel build lanes compile independently.
  rejected: Leaving package boundaries as a stated principle without a concrete file layout for build lanes to follow
  constraints: Build phase must create RecallScheduling and RecallCSV as real local SPM package targets, each with its own Swift Testing target
- [DEC-tech_specs-002] Stats aggregation (forecast/history/retention) runs in a dedicated background StatsComputationActor (@ModelActor) with its own read-only ModelContext, triggered by ModelContext.didSave notifications and publishing into a @MainActor @Observable StatsCache — explicitly named as a concurrency domain separate from the main-actor synchronous grade-save write path.
  rationale: Claude's addition: without this explicit separation, a builder reaching for the 'obviously simple' pattern would compute stats inline in a chart view's body, causing a full ReviewLog table scan on every re-render at the 300-3,000 card persona scale.
  rejected: Computing stats inline in view bodies or on the same main-actor write path as grade saves
  constraints: Any future performance pass may not merge StatsComputationActor's read path back onto the main-actor write path
- [DEC-tech_specs-003] UUID is the canonical identifier type across all cross-lane contracts (repositories, session snapshot queues, view models) — not SwiftData's PersistentIdentifier.
  rationale: Codex's interfaces-json used UUID throughout while Claude's used PersistentIdentifier; as coordinator this is resolved to UUID because letting PersistentIdentifier leak into primary_ui/view-model types would require SwiftData imports outside the persistence layer, breaking the layer separation the whole architecture is built to enforce.
  rejected: Using PersistentIdentifier as the canonical cross-lane identifier
  constraints: No primary_ui or services_utilities type may reference PersistentIdentifier directly; only the SwiftData repository implementations may translate between UUID and PersistentIdentifier internally
- [DEC-tech_specs-004] The review session snapshot queue must tolerate a stale/missing card ID at grading time (e.g. a card deleted between session start and being graded) by skipping it, incrementing a visible staleSkippedCount, and continuing — never crashing and never fabricating a grade or a silently-shrunk summary.
  rationale: Codex's Red Team catch: no prior phase named this edge case, and without an explicit test for it the app could still crash or silently misreport progress while claiming correctness, directly undermining the core trust promise.
  rejected: Leaving stale-ID handling as undefined/implicit behavior discovered during build; Treating a stale ID as a crash-worthy invariant violation
  constraints: Build/test phase must include a dedicated stale-ID mid-session skip test; Session summary UI must be able to surface staleSkippedCount if nonzero rather than hiding the discrepancy
- [DEC-tech_specs-005] CSVRowStatus is finalized as a concrete Swift enum with one case per malformed/duplicate/cap-blocked reason plus an ok case carrying the parsed front/back/note, replacing prose descriptions of the error taxonomy with a compiled shared contract type.
  rationale: Both contributors converged on the same taxonomy; encoding it as a real type (not a string or prose list) is what makes 'never silently drop a row' independently checkable by both the parser and the preview UI.
  rejected: Representing row status as a loosely-typed string/reason pair instead of an enum
  constraints: CSVParser.parseImportPreview and the import preview UI must both consume this exact enum, with no additional untyped error paths
- [DEC-tech_specs-006] Navigation uses typed per-tab route enums (StudyRoute, StatsRoute, SettingsRoute) instead of a type-erased NavigationPath.
  rationale: Claude's addition: gives parallel build lanes compile-time-checked routing instead of stringly-typed/type-erased paths that only fail at runtime.
  rejected: A single type-erased NavigationPath shared across all three tabs
  constraints: Each tab's NavigationStack must be driven by its own typed route array, not a shared NavigationPath
- [DEC-tech_specs-007] Plan-cap logic (deck/card counts vs. Free limits, StoreKit entitlement state) is centralized in one injected PlanGate object read by the card editor, CSV import preview, and deck creation flow.
  rationale: Claude's addition: prevents three independently-implemented cap counters from drifting out of sync, which would otherwise be a real risk given caps are checked from three separate UI entry points.
  rejected: Letting each cap-checking screen compute deck/card counts independently
  constraints: No screen may compute Free-tier cap state itself; all cap checks read from the single injected PlanGate instance
- [DEC-tech_specs-008] Optional hardware keyboard shortcuts (space/return to reveal; 1-4 or arrow keys to grade Again/Hard/Good/Easy) are added to the review session as an additive acceleration layered on top of the existing tap-based GradeStaircase, with a discoverable hint row.
  rationale: Claude's proposal: zero new frameworks, doesn't touch the locked non-color-dependent accessibility contract (VoiceOver/staircase labels remain the accessibility path of record), and is a direct, low-risk expression of the review-flow-speed priority for the daily, at-scale persona this app targets.
  rejected: Treating keyboard shortcuts as a replacement input path rather than additive; Deferring keyboard acceleration as out-of-scope polish
  constraints: Keyboard shortcuts must never be the sole way to satisfy the non-color-dependent grading accessibility requirement; VoiceOver labels and reduced-motion behavior must remain unchanged regardless of input method
- [DEC-tech_specs-009] Deck gains reminderHour/reminderMinute optional fields implementing per-deck Plus reminder-time override, and StatsSnapshot.retentionRate is typed as an optional Double (nil, not 0, when sampleSize is 0) to distinguish no-data from zero-retention.
  rationale: Concrete schema/type-level implementation of two already-locked requirements (per-deck reminder customization as a Plus differentiator; honest empty vs. sparse stats states) that needed an actual field/type decision to be buildable.

```swift
import UserNotifications

public struct ReminderScheduler: DayBoundaryCalculator {
    public func requestAuthorizationIfNeeded() async -> Bool {
        let center = UNUserNotificationCenter.current()
        var isAuthorized = false
        if #available(iOS 14.0, *) {
            let settings = await center.notificationSettings(for: .default)
            isAuthorized = settings.authorizationStatus == .authorized
            if !isAuthorized {
                let requestResult = await center.requestAuthorization(options: [.alert, .sound])
                isAuthorized = requestResult
            }
        } else {
            let settings = await center.getNotificationSettings()
            isAuthorized = settings.authorizationStatus == .authorized
            if !isAuthorized {
                let requestResult = await center.requestAuthorization(options: [.alert, .sound])
                isAuthorized = requestResult
            }
        }
        return isAuthorized
    }

    public func rescheduleForTomorrow(dueCount: Int, at time: DateComponents) async {
        guard dueCount > 0 else { return }
        
        let content = UNMutableNotificationContent()
        content.title = "Cards Due"
        content.body = "\(dueCount) cards are due today."
        
        var dateComponents = Calendar.current.dateComponents([.year, .month, .day], from: Date())
        dateComponents.hour = time.hour ?? 0
        dateComponents.minute = time.minute ?? 0
        
        let trigger = UNCalendarNotificationTrigger(dateMatching: dateComponents, repeats: false)
        let request = UNNotificationRequest(identifier: UUID().uuidString, content: content, trigger: trigger)
        
        await UNUserNotificationCenter.current().add(request)
    }

    public func cancelPending() async {
        await UNUserNotificationCenter.current().removeAllPendingNotificationRequests()
    }
    
    public func startOfTomorrow(relativeTo instant: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> Date {
        var components = calendar.dateComponents([.year, .month, .day], from: instant)
        components.day! += 1
        return calendar.date(from: components)!
    }
}
```

#### Implementation of ReminderService
```swift
import UserNotifications

public class ReminderService {
    private let scheduler: DayBoundaryCalculator
    
    public init(scheduler: DayBoundaryCalculator) {
        self.scheduler = scheduler
    }

    public func requestPermissionIfNeeded() async throws -> Bool {
        return try await scheduler.requestAuthorizationIfNeeded()
    }

    public func setReminder(enabled: Bool, atComponents: DateComponents?, deckID: UUID?) async throws {
        if enabled, let components = atComponents {
            // For now, fetchDueCount is a placeholder
            let dueCount = 10
            try await scheduler.rescheduleForTomorrow(dueCount: dueCount, at: components)
        } else {
            try await scheduler.cancelPending()
        }
    }

    public func refreshNotifications(now: Date) async throws {
        // For now, fetchDueCount is a placeholder
        let dueCount = 10

        if dueCount == 0 {
            try await scheduler.cancelPending()
        } else {
            try await setReminder(enabled: true, atComponents: DateComponents(), deckID: nil)
        }
    }
}
```

#### Explanation:
- **requestPermissionIfNeeded**: Requests notification permissions if not already granted.
- **setReminder**: Schedules or cancels notifications based on the `enabled` flag and the provided time components. It currently uses a hardcoded due count (`10`) as a placeholder.
- **refreshNotifications**: Checks the due count and cancels any pending notifications if the count is zero. Otherwise, it reschedules the notification.

# First-Party Apple Frameworks Cheatsheet (iOS 17+ / Swift 5.9+)

Build capable iPhone apps with **zero third-party dependencies**. For each framework: when to reach for it, the entry-point type, and a compilable, idiomatic snippet or the gotcha that bites people. All examples target **iOS 17 minimum** unless a call-out says otherwise; Swift Concurrency (`async`/`await`) is preferred over completion handlers everywhere Apple offers it.

## General rules

- **Prefer these over SPM packages.** RevenueCat, Firebase Analytics, Lottie, Alamofire, etc. all have first-party equivalents good enough for most apps. Fewer deps = smaller binary, faster builds, no supply-chain risk, no privacy-manifest surprises.
- **Every framework that touches user data needs an `Info.plist` usage-description string** (or an entitlement). Missing it is a runtime crash the moment the API is used — not a compile error. The specific keys are listed per section.
- **Import the framework and its SwiftUI companion when one exists** (e.g. `import MapKit` gives you `Map`; `import StoreKit` gives you `SubscriptionStoreView`/`StoreView`).
- **Do capability checks before hardware-dependent APIs** (`CHHapticEngine.capabilitiesForHardware().supportsHaptics`, `HKHealthStore.isHealthDataAvailable()`, `GKLocalPlayer.local.isAuthenticated`). Simulators and older/cheaper devices lie.
- **Never block the main actor.** Long queries, audio-graph setup, and StoreKit calls belong in `Task {}` or `async` functions.
- **Verify APIs against the deployment target.** Several SwiftUI conveniences (e.g. `GameCenterView`, Control widgets) shipped *after* iOS 17. Availability call-outs below flag these.

---

## StoreKit 2 — In-App Purchase & Subscriptions

**Use it when:** you sell anything — consumables, non-consumables, or auto-renewable subscriptions. Replaces callback-based StoreKit 1 entirely.

**Start from:** `Product` (fetch + purchase) and `Transaction` (entitlements + history). No server strictly required — signatures are verified on-device via `VerificationResult`.

### The three things you must do

1. **Load products by ID** (IDs come from App Store Connect):

```swift
import StoreKit

let productIDs = ["com.app.pro.monthly", "com.app.pro.yearly", "com.app.coins.100"]
let products = try await Product.products(for: productIDs)   // async throws
```

2. **Purchase, then verify and finish the transaction:**

```swift
func purchase(_ product: Product) async throws -> Transaction? {
    let result = try await product.purchase()
    switch result {
    case .success(let verification):
        let transaction = try checkVerified(verification)
        await transaction.finish()          // REQUIRED — unfinished txns replay forever
        return transaction
    case .userCancelled, .pending:
        return nil
    @unknown default:
        return nil
    }
}

func checkVerified<T>(_ result: VerificationResult<T>) throws -> T {
    switch result {
    case .unverified(_, let error): throw error   // signature failed — do NOT grant
    case .verified(let safe):       return safe
    }
}
```

3. **Listen for `Transaction.updates` from app launch** — the single most-missed requirement. It catches renewals, Ask-to-Buy approvals, refunds, and purchases made on other devices.

```swift
// Start this in your App init / a top-level task and keep it alive for the app's lifetime.
func observeTransactions() -> Task<Void, Never> {
    Task.detached {
        for await update in Transaction.updates {
            guard case .verified(let transaction) = update else { continue }
            await grantEntitlement(for: transaction)   // your unlock logic
            await transaction.finish()
        }
    }
}
```

### Checking what the user currently owns

Use `Transaction.currentEntitlements` (an async sequence). **iOS 18.4+ note:** the per-product `Transaction.currentEntitlement(for:)` is deprecated in favor of `Transaction.currentEntitlements(for:)`, because a user can hold multiple entitling transactions (e.g. own it *and* have Family Sharing access).

```swift
func hasActiveSubscription() async -> Bool {
    for await result in Transaction.currentEntitlements {
        guard case .verified(let transaction) = result else { continue }
        if transaction.productType == .autoRenewable && transaction.revocationDate == nil {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}
```

### Subscription status & renewal info

```swift
// groupID = the subscription group configured in App Store Connect
let statuses = try await Product.SubscriptionInfo.status(for: subscriptionGroupID)
for status in statuses {
    guard case .verified(let renewalInfo) = status.renewalInfo else { continue }
    let willAutoRenew = renewalInfo.willAutoRenew   // false => user cancelled, still in period
    _ = (status.state, willAutoRenew)               // .subscribed, .expired, .inGracePeriod, ...
}
```

### Drop-in SwiftUI storefront (iOS 17+)

Skip building a custom paywall — these render Apple's native UI:

```swift
import SwiftUI
import StoreKit

// Whole subscription group with a marketing header:
SubscriptionStoreView(groupID: subscriptionGroupID) {
    VStack { Text("Unlock Pro").font(.largeTitle.bold()) }
}
.subscriptionStoreControlStyle(.prominentPicker)

// Non-subscription products:
StoreView(ids: ["com.app.coins.100", "com.app.coins.500"])
```

- **Test locally with a `.storekit` configuration file** (Xcode → File → New → File → StoreKit Configuration). Lets you buy, refund, and fast-forward renewals in the simulator with no sandbox account.
- `await transaction.finish()` is mandatory — forgetting it makes the transaction reappear in `Transaction.updates` every launch.
- **Always ship a "Restore Purchases" button** for non-consumables/subscriptions (App Review requirement). Call `try await AppStore.sync()`, then re-scan `currentEntitlements`.

public enum SM2Engine {
    public static func schedule(current: SchedulingState, grade: Grade) -> SchedulingState {
        let quality = grade.quality
        let adjustedEaseFactor = max(1.3, current.easeFactor + easeFactorDelta(for: quality))
        let wasLapse = quality.rawValue < 3

        guard !wasLapse else {
            return SchedulingState(
                easeFactor: adjustedEaseFactor,
                intervalDays: 1,
                repetitionCount: 0
            )
        }

        let nextRepetitions = current.repetitionCount + 1
        let intervalDays: Int
        if current.repetitionCount <= 0 {
            intervalDays = 1
        } else if current.repetitionCount == 1 {
            intervalDays = 6
        } else {
            intervalDays = max(1, Int((Double(current.intervalDays) * adjustedEaseFactor).rounded()))
        }

        return SchedulingState(
            easeFactor: adjustedEaseFactor,
            intervalDays: intervalDays,
            repetitionCount: nextRepetitions
        )
    }

    public static func isDue(dueDate: Date, now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> Bool {
        dueDate < startOfTomorrow(now: now, calendar: calendar)
    }

    public static func startOfTomorrow(now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> Date {
        let startOfToday = calendar.startOfDay(for: now)
        return calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: 1, to: startOfToday) ?? now
    }

    public static func transition(
        current: SM2CardState,
        grade: Grade,
        at now: Date,
        calendar: Calendar
    ) -> SM2TransitionResult {
        let next = schedule(
            current: SchedulingState(
                easeFactor: current.easeFactor,
                intervalDays: current.intervalDays,
                repetitionCount: current.repetitionCount
            ),
            grade: grade
        )
        let nextDue = calculateNextDueDate(
            from: now,
            intervalDays: next.intervalDays,
            calendar: calendar
        )
        let elapsedDays = max(
            0,
            calendar.dateComponents([.day], from: current.dueDate, to: now).day ?? 0
        )

        return SM2TransitionResult(
            next: SM2CardState(
                cardID: current.cardID,
                easeFactor: next.easeFactor,
                intervalDays: next.intervalDays,
                repetitionCount: next.repetitionCount,
                dueDate: nextDue
            ),
            grade: grade.quality,
            elapsedDays: elapsedDays
        )
    }

    public static func calculateNextDueDate(from date: Date, intervalDays: Int, calendar: Calendar) -> Date {
        let interval = max(1, intervalDays)
        let startOfToday = calendar.startOfDay(for: date)
        return calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: interval, to: startOfToday) ?? date
    }

    public static func lapseResult(current: SM2CardState, at now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> SM2TransitionResult {
        transition(current: current, grade: .again, at: now, calendar: calendar)
    }

    public static func wasLapse(grade: Grade) -> Bool {
        grade.rawValue < 3
    }

    private static func easeFactorDelta(for quality: SM2Quality) -> Double {
        let q = Double(5 - quality.rawValue)
        return 0.1 - q * (0.08 + q * 0.02)
    }
}

    private let service: ReviewSessionService
    private let clock: () -> Date

        guard currentIndex < queue.count else { return nil }
        return queue[currentIndex]
    }

        currentIndex >= queue.count
    }

    public init(plan: ReviewSessionPlan, service: ReviewSessionService, clock: @escaping () -> Date = Date.init) {

            }
        } catch {
            staleSkippedCount += 1
        }
        advance()
    }

        currentIndex = queue.count
    }

    private func advance() {
        currentIndex += 1
        isRevealed = false
    }

extension SessionScope: Hashable {
    public static func == (lhs: SessionScope, rhs: SessionScope) -> Bool {
        switch (lhs, rhs) {
        case let (.singleDeck(a), .singleDeck(b)):
            return a == b
        case (.allDecks, .allDecks):

        default:

        switch self {
        case .singleDeck(let id):
            hasher.combine(0)
            hasher.combine(id)
        case .allDecks:
            hasher.combine(1)
        }
    }

struct DeckEditorView: View {

    let onSave: (String) async throws -> Void

    @State private var name: String
    @State private var isSaving = false
    @State private var errorMessage: String?
    @FocusState private var isNameFocused: Bool

    init(initialName: String = "", onSave: @escaping (String) async throws -> Void) {
        self.initialName = initialName
        self.onSave = onSave
        _name = State(initialValue: initialName)
    }

    private var trimmedName: String {
        name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
    }

    private var canSave: Bool {
        !trimmedName.isEmpty && !isSaving
    }

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            Form {
                Section {
                    TextField("Deck name", text: $name)
                        .focused($isNameFocused)
                        .submitLabel(.done)
                        .disabled(isSaving)
                        .onSubmit(save)
                        .accessibilityIdentifier("deckEditor.nameField")
                } footer: {
                    if let errorMessage {
                        Text(errorMessage)
                            .foregroundStyle(DS.Palette.danger)
                    }
                }
            }
            .navigationTitle(initialName.isEmpty ? "New Deck" : "Rename Deck")
            .toolbar {
                ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction) {
                    Button("Cancel") { dismiss() }
                        .disabled(isSaving)
                        .accessibilityIdentifier("deckEditor.cancelButton")
                }
                ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) {
                    if isSaving {
                        ProgressView()
                            .accessibilityIdentifier("deckEditor.saving")
                    } else {
                        Button("Save", action: save)
                            .disabled(!canSave)
                            .accessibilityIdentifier("deckEditor.saveButton")
                    }
                }
            }
            .onAppear { isNameFocused = true }
        }
    }

    private func save() {
        guard canSave else { return }
        isSaving = true
        errorMessage = nil
        Task {
            do {
                try await onSave(trimmedName)
                dismiss()
            } catch {
                isSaving = false
                errorMessage = "Couldn't save this deck. Try again."

        initialNote: String = "",
        onSave: @escaping (_ front: String, _ back: String, _ note: String?) async throws -> Void
    ) {
        self.initialFront = initialFront
        self.initialBack = initialBack
        self.initialNote = initialNote
        self.onSave = onSave
        _front = State(initialValue: initialFront)
        _back = State(initialValue: initialBack)
        _note = State(initialValue: initialNote)
    }

    private var trimmedFront: String { front.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }
    private var trimmedBack: String { back.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }
    private var trimmedNote: String { note.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }

    private var canSave: Bool {
        !trimmedFront.isEmpty && !trimmedBack.isEmpty && !isSaving
    }

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            Form {
                Section("Front") {
                    TextField("Front of card", text: $front, axis: .vertical)
                        .focused($focusedField, equals: .front)
                        .submitLabel(.next)
                        .disabled(isSaving)
                        .onSubmit { focusedField = .back }
                        .accessibilityIdentifier("cardEditor.frontField")
                }
                Section("Back") {
                    TextField("Back of card", text: $back, axis: .vertical)
                        .focused($focusedField, equals: .back)
                        .submitLabel(.next)
                        .disabled(isSaving)
                        .onSubmit { focusedField = .note }
                        .accessibilityIdentifier("cardEditor.backField")
                }
                Section("Note (optional)") {
                    TextField("Extra context", text: $note, axis: .vertical)
                        .focused($focusedField, equals: .note)
                        .submitLabel(.done)
                        .disabled(isSaving)
                        .onSubmit(save)
                        .accessibilityIdentifier("cardEditor.noteField")
                }
                if let errorMessage {
                    Section {
                        Text(errorMessage)
                            .foregroundStyle(DS.Palette.danger)
                    }
                }
            }
            .navigationTitle(initialFront.isEmpty ? "New Card" : "Edit Card")
            .toolbar {
                ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction) {
                    Button("Cancel") { dismiss() }
                        .disabled(isSaving)
                        .accessibilityIdentifier("cardEditor.cancelButton")
                }
                ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) {
                    if isSaving {
                        ProgressView()
                            .accessibilityIdentifier("cardEditor.saving")
                    } else {
                        Button("Save", action: save)
                            .disabled(!canSave)
                            .accessibilityIdentifier("cardEditor.saveButton")
                    }
                }
            }
            .onAppear { focusedField = .front }
        }
    }

    private func save() {
        guard canSave else { return }
        isSaving = true
        errorMessage = nil
        Task {
            do {
                try await onSave(trimmedFront, trimmedBack, trimmedNote.isEmpty ? nil : trimmedNote)
                dismiss()
            } catch {
                isSaving = false
                errorMessage = "Couldn't save this card. Try again."
            }
        }
    }

public struct ReviewCountPoint: Equatable, Sendable {
    public let date: Date
    public let reviewCount: Int
    public let againCount: Int

    public init(date: Date, reviewCount: Int, againCount: Int) {
        self.date = date
        self.reviewCount = reviewCount
        self.againCount = againCount
    }

public enum ReviewLogGrade: Int {
    case again = 2
    case hard = 3
    case good = 4
    case easy = 5
}

public func computeReviewHistory(
    logs: [ReviewLogEntry],
    now: Date,
    windowInDays: Int,
    demoFilter: DemoSeedFilter = .none,
    calendar: Calendar = .current
) -> [ReviewCountPoint] {
    guard windowInDays > 0 else { return [] }

    let effectiveLogs = filterNonDemoReviewLogs(logs, demoFilter: demoFilter)

    let start = calendar.startOfDay(for: now)
    let firstDay = calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: -(windowInDays - 1), to: start) ?? start

    let clampedLogs = effectiveLogs.filter { log in
        log.timestamp >= firstDay && log.timestamp <= now
    }

    var countsByDay: [Date: (reviews: Int, again: Int)] = [:]

    for log in clampedLogs {
        let bucket = calendar.startOfDay(for: log.timestamp)
        var bucketValue = countsByDay[bucket] ?? (reviews: 0, again: 0)
        bucketValue.reviews += 1
        if log.grade == ReviewLogGrade.again.rawValue {
            bucketValue.again += 1
        }
        countsByDay[bucket] = bucketValue
    }

    return (0..<windowInDays).compactMap { offset in
        guard let date = calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: offset, to: firstDay) else { return nil }
        let bucket = countsByDay[date] ?? (reviews: 0, again: 0)
        return ReviewCountPoint(date: date, reviewCount: bucket.reviews, againCount: bucket.again)
    }
}

) -> [ReviewCountPoint] {
    let effectiveLogs: [ReviewLogEntry]

    )
}

import Foundation

public struct RetentionResult: Equatable, Sendable {
    public let retentionRatePercent: Double
    public let gradedTotal: Int
    public let goodOrEasyCount: Int

    public init(retentionRatePercent: Double, gradedTotal: Int, goodOrEasyCount: Int) {
        self.retentionRatePercent = retentionRatePercent
        self.gradedTotal = gradedTotal
        self.goodOrEasyCount = goodOrEasyCount
    }
}

public func retentionRate(logs: [ReviewLogEntry], from: Date, to: Date) -> RetentionResult {
    return retentionRate(logs: logs, from: from, to: to, demoFilter: .none)
}

public func retentionRate(
    logs: [ReviewLogEntry],
    from: Date,
    to: Date,
    demoFilter: DemoSeedFilter
) -> RetentionResult {
    let effectiveLogs = filterNonDemoReviewLogs(logs, demoFilter: demoFilter)

    guard from <= to else {
        return RetentionResult(retentionRatePercent: 0.0, gradedTotal: 0, goodOrEasyCount: 0)
    }

    let scoped = effectiveLogs.filter { $0.timestamp >= from && $0.timestamp <= to }
    let gradedTotal = scoped.count

    guard gradedTotal > 0 else {
        return RetentionResult(retentionRatePercent: 0.0, gradedTotal: 0, goodOrEasyCount: 0)
    }

    let passCount = scoped.filter { log in
        log.grade == ReviewLogGrade.good.rawValue || log.grade == ReviewLogGrade.easy.rawValue
    }.count

    let rate = (Double(passCount) / Double(gradedTotal)) * 100
    return RetentionResult(retentionRatePercent: rate, gradedTotal: gradedTotal, goodOrEasyCount: passCount)
}

public struct StreakResult: Equatable, Sendable {
    public let currentStreakDays: Int
    public let lastReviewDate: Date?

    public init(currentStreakDays: Int, lastReviewDate: Date?) {
        self.currentStreakDays = currentStreakDays
        self.lastReviewDate = lastReviewDate
    }
}

public func reviewStreakDays(
    logs: [ReviewLogEntry],
    now: Date,
    calendar: Calendar = .current,
    demoFilter: DemoSeedFilter = .none
) -> StreakResult {
    return reviewStreakDays(
        logs: logs,
        deckIDByCardID: nil,
        now: now,
        calendar: calendar,
        demoFilter: demoFilter
    )
}

public func reviewStreakDays(
    logs: [ReviewLogEntry],
    deckIDByCardID: [UUID: UUID]?,
    now: Date,
    calendar: Calendar = .current,
    demoFilter: DemoSeedFilter = .none
) -> StreakResult {
    let effective: [ReviewLogEntry]
    if let deckIDByCardID {
        effective = filterNonDemoReviewLogs(logs, demoFilter: demoFilter, deckIDByCardID: deckIDByCardID)
    } else {
        effective = filterNonDemoReviewLogs(logs, demoFilter: demoFilter)
    }

    guard !effective.isEmpty else {
        return StreakResult(currentStreakDays: 0, lastReviewDate: nil)
    }

    let reviewDays = Set(effective.map { calendar.startOfDay(for: $0.timestamp) })
    guard let newestReviewDay = reviewDays.max() else {
        return StreakResult(currentStreakDays: 0, lastReviewDate: nil)
    }

    let today = calendar.startOfDay(for: now)
    var streak = 1

    var cursor = newestReviewDay
    while true {
        guard let previousDay = calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: -1, to: cursor) else {
            break
        }

        if reviewDays.contains(previousDay) {
            streak += 1
            cursor = previousDay
            continue
        }

        break
    }

    if newestReviewDay > today {
        return StreakResult(currentStreakDays: 0, lastReviewDate: newestReviewDay)
    }

    return StreakResult(currentStreakDays: streak, lastReviewDate: newestReviewDay)
}

import Foundation

public struct DemoSeedFilter: Equatable, Sendable {
    public let demoDeckIDs: Set<UUID>
    public let demoCardIDs: Set<UUID>

    public init(demoDeckIDs: Set<UUID> = [], demoCardIDs: Set<UUID> = []) {
        self.demoDeckIDs = demoDeckIDs
        self.demoCardIDs = demoCardIDs
    }

    public static var none: DemoSeedFilter {
        DemoSeedFilter()
    }

    public func isDemoDeck(_ id: UUID) -> Bool {
        demoDeckIDs.contains(id)
    }

    public func isDemoCard(_ id: UUID) -> Bool {
        demoCardIDs.contains(id)
    }

    public func isDemoCardEntry(_ cardID: UUID, belongingTo deckID: UUID?) -> Bool {
        isDemoCard(cardID) || (deckID.map { isDemoDeck($0) } ?? false)
    }
}

public func filterNonDemoReviewLogs(
    _ logs: [ReviewLogEntry],
    demoFilter: DemoSeedFilter
) -> [ReviewLogEntry] {
    guard !demoFilter.demoCardIDs.isEmpty || !demoFilter.demoDeckIDs.isEmpty else {
        return logs
    }

    return logs.filter { log in
        !demoFilter.isDemoCard(log.cardId)
    }
}

public func filterNonDemoReviewLogs(
    _ logs: [ReviewLogEntry],
    demoFilter: DemoSeedFilter,
    deckIDByCardID: [UUID: UUID]
) -> [ReviewLogEntry] {
    guard !demoFilter.demoCardIDs.isEmpty || !demoFilter.demoDeckIDs.isEmpty else {
        return logs
    }

    return logs.filter { log in
        let deckID = deckIDByCardID[log.cardId]
        return !demoFilter.isDemoCardEntry(log.cardId, belongingTo: deckID)
    }
}

public final class DefaultModelContainerManager: ModelContainerManager {
    public private(set) var container: ModelContainer?
    public private(set) var isRecoveredState: Bool = false

    public init() {}

    public func start() throws -> ModelContainer {

        let descriptor: FetchDescriptor<Card>

        if let forDeck {
            descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Card>(
                predicate: #Predicate { card in
                    card.dueDate < boundary && card.deck?.id == forDeck && (includeArchived || card.deck?.archivedAt == nil)

            )
        }

        return try context.fetch(descriptor)
    }

            for deckID in deckIDs {
                let due = try cardRepository(at: now, deckID: deckID)

            easeFactor: card.easeFactor,
            intervalDays: card.intervalDays,
            repetitionCount: card.repetitionCount
        )
        let nextState = SM2Engine.schedule(current: currentState, grade: grade)
        let nextDue = SM2Engine.calculateNextDueDate(from: now, intervalDays: nextState.intervalDays, calendar: .current)

            timestamp: now,
            grade: grade.rawValue,
            easeFactorBefore: card.easeFactor,
            easeFactorAfter: nextState.easeFactor,
            intervalBefore: card.intervalDays,
            intervalAfter: nextState.intervalDays,
            repetitionBefore: card.repetitionCount,
            repetitionAfter: nextState.repetitionCount,
            card: card
        )

        card.easeFactor = nextState.easeFactor
        card.intervalDays = nextState.intervalDays
        card.repetitionCount = nextState.repetitionCount
        card.lastReviewedAt = now
        card.dueDate = nextDue

        context.insert(reviewLog)

        do {
            try context.save()
            return GradeOutcome(state: nextState, dueDate: nextDue, wasLapse: grade.rawValue < 3)
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

        let trimmedBack = back.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        guard !trimmedFront.isEmpty, !trimmedBack.isEmpty else {

        }

        let now = Date()
        let card = Card(

            back: trimmedBack,
            note: note?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines),
            dueDate: now,
            deck: deck,
            isDemo: deck.isDemo,
            createdAt: now
        )

        context.insert(card)
        do {
            try context.save()
            return card
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

        guard let card = try card(by: id) else {
            throw RecallDataError.notFound
        }

        context.delete(card)
        do {
            try context.save()
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

        return try context.fetch(descriptor).first
    }

    private func deck(by id: UUID) throws -> Deck? {
        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Deck>(predicate: #Predicate { $0.id == id })
        return try context.fetch(descriptor).first
    }

    private func cardRepository(at instant: Date, deckID: UUID?) throws -> [Card] {

                card.dueDate < boundary && card.deck?.archivedAt == nil
            },
            sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\\Card.dueDate, order: .forward)]
        )
        return try context.fetch(descriptor)
    }

public final class DefaultModelContainerManager: ModelContainerManager {
    public private(set) var container: ModelContainer?
    public private(set) var isRecoveredState: Bool = false

    public init() {}

    public func start() throws -> ModelContainer {
        if let existing = container {
            isRecoveredState = false
            return existing
        }

        switch ModelContainerFactory.makeContainer() {
        case .success(let created):

        guard let deck = try fetchDeck(id: deckID) else {

        }

        let trimmedFront = front.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        let trimmedBack = back.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        guard !trimmedFront.isEmpty, !trimmedBack.isEmpty else {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: "Card front and back must not be empty.")
        }

        let now = Date()
        let card = Card(
            front: trimmedFront,
            back: trimmedBack,
            note: note?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines),
            dueDate: now,
            deck: deck,
            isDemo: deck.isDemo,
            createdAt: now
        )

        context.insert(card)

        do {
            try context.save()
            return card
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

    private func cardsDueSync(at instant: Date, calendar: Calendar, forDeck: UUID?, includeArchived: Bool) throws -> [Card] {
        let boundary = SM2Engine.startOfTomorrow(now: instant, calendar: calendar)

        let descriptor: FetchDescriptor<Card>
        if let forDeck {
            descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Card>(
                predicate: #Predicate { card in
                    card.dueDate < boundary &&
                    card.deck?.id == forDeck &&
                    (includeArchived || card.deck?.archivedAt == nil)
                },
                sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\Card.dueDate, order: .forward)]
            )
        } else {
            descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Card>(
                predicate: #Predicate { card in
                    card.dueDate < boundary && (includeArchived || card.deck?.archivedAt == nil)
                },
                sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\Card.dueDate, order: .forward)]
            )
        }

        return try context.fetch(descriptor)
    }

    }

        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Deck>(predicate: #Predicate { $0.id == id })
        return try context.fetch(descriptor).first
    }

+public final class DefaultModelContainerManager: ModelContainerManager {
+    public private(set) var container: ModelContainer?
+    public private(set) var isRecoveredState: Bool = false
+
+    public init() {}
+
+    public func start() throws -> ModelContainer {
+        if let existing = container {
+            isRecoveredState = false
+            return existing
+        }
+
+        switch ModelContainerFactory.makeContainer() {
+        case .success(let created):
+            container = created
+            isRecoveredState = false
+            return created
+        case .failure(let error):
+            isRecoveredState = true
+            throw error
+        }

// MARK: - Container manager

public final class DefaultModelContainerManager: ModelContainerManager {
    public private(set) var container: ModelContainer?
    public private(set) var isRecoveredState: Bool = false

    public init() {}

    public func start() throws -> ModelContainer {
        if let existing = container {
            isRecoveredState = false
            return existing
        }

        switch ModelContainerFactory.makeContainer() {
        case .success(let created):
            container = created
            isRecoveredState = false
            return created
        case .failure(let error):
            isRecoveredState = true
            throw error
        }
    }
}

                sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\Card.dueDate, order: .forward)]

        }

        return try context.fetch(descriptor)
    }

    }

        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Deck>(predicate: #Predicate { $0.id == id })
        return try context.fetch(descriptor).first
    }

public final class SwiftDataReviewRepository: ReviewRepository {
    private let context: ModelContext

    public init(context: ModelContext) {
        self.context = context
    }

    public func fetchDueCards(deckIDs: [UUID]?, now: Date) throws -> [Card] {
        if let deckIDs, deckIDs.isEmpty {
            return []
        }

        if let deckIDs {
            var allDue: [Card] = []
            for deckID in deckIDs {
                let due = try cardRepository(at: now, deckID: deckID)
                allDue.append(contentsOf: due)
            }
            return allDue.sorted { $0.dueDate < $1.dueDate }
        }

        return try cardRepository(at: now, deckID: nil)
    }

    public func recordGrade(cardID: UUID, grade: Grade, now: Date) throws -> GradeOutcome {
        guard let card = try card(by: cardID) else {
            throw RecallDataError.notFound
        }

        let currentState = SchedulingState(
            easeFactor: card.easeFactor,
            intervalDays: card.intervalDays,
            repetitionCount: card.repetitionCount
        )
        let nextState = SM2Engine.schedule(current: currentState, grade: grade)
        let nextDue = SM2Engine.calculateNextDueDate(from: now, intervalDays: nextState.intervalDays, calendar: .current)

        let reviewLog = ReviewLog(
            timestamp: now,
            grade: grade.rawValue,
            easeFactorBefore: card.easeFactor,
            easeFactorAfter: nextState.easeFactor,
            intervalBefore: card.intervalDays,
            intervalAfter: nextState.intervalDays,
            repetitionBefore: card.repetitionCount,
            repetitionAfter: nextState.repetitionCount,
            card: card
        )

        card.easeFactor = nextState.easeFactor
        card.intervalDays = nextState.intervalDays
        card.repetitionCount = nextState.repetitionCount
        card.lastReviewedAt = now
        card.dueDate = nextDue

        context.insert(reviewLog)

        do {
            try context.save()
            return GradeOutcome(state: nextState, dueDate: nextDue, wasLapse: grade.rawValue < 3)
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

    public func createCard(front: String, back: String, note: String?, deckID: UUID) throws -> Card {
        guard let deck = try deck(by: deckID) else {
            throw RecallDataError.notFound
        }

        let trimmedFront = front.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        let trimmedBack = back.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        guard !trimmedFront.isEmpty, !trimmedBack.isEmpty else {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: "Card front and back must not be empty.")
        }

        let now = Date()
        let card = Card(
            front: trimmedFront,
            back: trimmedBack,
            note: note?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines),
            dueDate: now,
            deck: deck,
            isDemo: deck.isDemo,
            createdAt: now
        )

        context.insert(card)
        do {
            try context.save()
            return card
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

    public func deleteCard(id: UUID) throws {
        guard let card = try card(by: id) else {
            throw RecallDataError.notFound
        }

        context.delete(card)
        do {
            try context.save()
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

    private func card(by id: UUID) throws -> Card? {
        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Card>(predicate: #Predicate { $0.id == id })
        return try context.fetch(descriptor).first
    }

    private func deck(by id: UUID) throws -> Deck? {
        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Deck>(predicate: #Predicate { $0.id == id })
        return try context.fetch(descriptor).first
    }

    private func cardRepository(at instant: Date, deckID: UUID?) throws -> [Card] {
        let boundary = SM2Engine.startOfTomorrow(now: instant, calendar: .current)
        if let deckID {
            let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Card>(
                predicate: #Predicate {
                    $0.dueDate < boundary &&
                    $0.deck?.id == deckID &&
                    $0.deck?.archivedAt == nil
                },
                sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\Card.dueDate, order: .forward)]
            )
            return try context.fetch(descriptor)
        }

        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Card>(
            predicate: #Predicate { card in
                card.dueDate < boundary && card.deck?.archivedAt == nil
            },
            sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\Card.dueDate, order: .forward)]
        )
        return try context.fetch(descriptor)
    }
}

    }
}

public enum SM2Engine {
    public static func schedule(current: SchedulingState, grade: Grade) -> SchedulingState {
        let quality = grade.quality
        let adjustedEaseFactor = max(1.3, current.easeFactor + easeFactorDelta(for: quality))
        let wasLapse = quality.rawValue < 3

        guard !wasLapse else {
            return SchedulingState(
                easeFactor: adjustedEaseFactor,
                intervalDays: 1,
                repetitionCount: 0
            )
        }

        let nextRepetitions = current.repetitionCount + 1
        let intervalDays: Int
        if current.repetitionCount <= 0 {
            intervalDays = 1
        } else if current.repetitionCount == 1 {
            intervalDays = 6
        } else {
            intervalDays = max(1, Int((Double(current.intervalDays) * adjustedEaseFactor).rounded()))
        }

        return SchedulingState(
            easeFactor: adjustedEaseFactor,
            intervalDays: intervalDays,
            repetitionCount: nextRepetitions
        )
    }

    public static func isDue(dueDate: Date, now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> Bool {
        dueDate < startOfTomorrow(now: now, calendar: calendar)
    }

    public static func startOfTomorrow(now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> Date {
        let startOfToday = calendar.startOfDay(for: now)
        return calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: 1, to: startOfToday) ?? now
    }

    public static func transition(
        current: SM2CardState,
        grade: Grade,
        at now: Date,
        calendar: Calendar
    ) -> SM2TransitionResult {
        let next = schedule(
            current: SchedulingState(
                easeFactor: current.easeFactor,
                intervalDays: current.intervalDays,
                repetitionCount: current.repetitionCount
            ),
            grade: grade
        )
        let nextDue = calculateNextDueDate(
            from: now,
            intervalDays: next.intervalDays,
            calendar: calendar
        )
        let elapsedDays = max(
            0,
            calendar.dateComponents([.day], from: current.dueDate, to: now).day ?? 0
        )

        return SM2TransitionResult(
            next: SM2CardState(
                cardID: current.cardID,
                easeFactor: next.easeFactor,
                intervalDays: next.intervalDays,
                repetitionCount: next.repetitionCount,
                dueDate: nextDue
            ),
            grade: grade.quality,
            elapsedDays: elapsedDays
        )
    }

    public static func calculateNextDueDate(from date: Date, intervalDays: Int, calendar: Calendar) -> Date {
        let interval = max(1, intervalDays)
        let startOfToday = calendar.startOfDay(for: date)
        return calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: interval, to: startOfToday) ?? date
    }

    public static func lapseResult(current: SM2CardState, at now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> SM2TransitionResult {
        transition(current: current, grade: .again, at: now, calendar: calendar)
    }

    public static func wasLapse(grade: Grade) -> Bool {
        grade.rawValue < 3
    }

    private static func easeFactorDelta(for quality: SM2Quality) -> Double {
        let q = Double(5 - quality.rawValue)
        return 0.1 - q * (0.08 + q * 0.02)
    }
}
